newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel weighs transfer of taxes to Palestinians.
newsitem.headline: Israel weighs transfer of taxes to Palestinians.

text.p: Israel's Finance Ministry is considering the possibility of transferring to the Palestinian Authority purchase tax collected on goods bought in Israel, a senior ministry official said on Thursday.

"The Palestinian request (that purchase taxes be transferred to them) is a significant change in the Paris economic agreement," said Aryeh Zaeff, head of customs and value added tax (VAT) at the Finance Ministry.

"There are talks within the Treasury on this issue. There is a certain legitimacy to their request. I believe we will find a solution," he said speaking at a meeting of Israeli businessmen on trade with Palestinians.
Purchase taxes are levied on most goods including imports. Under the 1994 economic agreement, Israel transfers VAT and customs collected from Palestinians.

Zaeff said Israel was prepared to negotiate the issue of purchase tax, on condition the Palestinian Authority does not prohibit Israeli franchises of international companies from selling their products in the self-ruled areas. Zaeff said this was a breach of the economic agreement.

Israel is disputing a Palestinian decision to stop Israeli franchises of international companies from selling products in the West Bank and Gaza to encourage Palestinian companies to replace them. This is due to take effect on October 1.
The Federation of Israeli Chambers of Commerce, which organised Thursday's meeting, says this move violates the economic agreement and in effect is a boycott on Israel.
Israel and the Palestinians signed an agreement in 1994 establishing a free trade area between Israel and the Palestinian self-rule areas.
Zaeff said the economic agreement is working well and benefits both Israel and the Palestinians. "It is only natural that a few years after the agreement was signed the two sides sit and discuss it."
